title: A two-sided dual reverses a prescribed Tor interval
statement: Let C be a braided closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions, and choose D(C) with its canonical K-flat derived tensor. Let K,L in D(C) have exact pairings L,K and K,L. If K has Tor amplitude [a,b], then L has Tor amplitude [-b,-a]. Here Tor amplitude [r,s] means that tensoring with any object F of C placed in degree zero has cohomology only in [r,s]. No ordering or boundedness hypothesis beyond the stated amplitude is required.

proof.text: For a degree-zero object F, test L tensor F against the orthogonal descriptions of the standard t-structure. If Y is below -b, duality identifies maps Y to L tensor F with maps K tensor Y to F; the upper Tor bound makes their source concentrated below degree zero, so these maps vanish. If Y is above -a, the other exact pairing identifies maps L tensor F to Y with maps F to K tensor Y; the lower Tor bound again makes them vanish. The two orthogonality criteria give the reflected interval.
